scope: Four exact API DLL names; no wildcard, deployment or runtime exemption

systemDirectory.quote: The %windir%\System32 directory is reserved for 64-bit applications on 64-bit Windows.
systemDirectory.runtimePolicy: Require the observed absolute module path below System32, SysWOW64 or WinSxS; app-local copies remain rejected.

authz.dll.requirementsQuote: Minimum supported client: Windows XP [desktop apps only]; Minimum supported server: Windows Server 2003 [desktop apps only]; DLL: Authz.dll

netapi32.dll.requirementsQuote: Minimum supported client: Windows 2000 Professional [desktop apps only]; Minimum supported server: Windows 2000 Server [desktop apps only]; DLL: Netapi32.dll

uiautomationcore.dll.requirementsQuote: Minimum supported client: Windows XP [desktop apps; Minimum supported server: Windows Server 2003 [desktop apps; DLL: Uiautomationcore.dll
uiautomationcore.dll.note: The published requirements table has a truncated desktop-app suffix. Newer individual UI Automation APIs can require newer Windows versions; this is not a whole-product minimum-OS certification.

xmllite.dll.minimumClient: Windows Vista or later; also Windows XP with Service Pack 3 or later
xmllite.dll.minimumServer: Windows Server 2008 or later; also Windows Server 2003 with Service Pack 2 or later
xmllite.dll.requirementsQuote: The XmlLite runtime file, Xmllite.dll, is integrated into the following operating systems and products: Windows Server 2008 or later; Windows Vista or later; Windows XP with Service Pack 3 or later; Windows Server 2003 with Service Pack 2 or later.
xmllite.dll.deploymentQuote: The XmlLite runtime is maintained by the Windows Update service. You cannot redistribute the Xmllite.dll file with your application.

limitations: Documentation establishes these exact OS API library identities, not actual loaded-module observations.
Minimum OS values describe representative APIs, not the complete launcher or every imported symbol.
Forbidden engines, dynamic compiler runtimes, unknown names and app-local system-name DLL copies remain rejected.
No signatures or runtime results are fabricated when the host signature command is unavailable.
